purpose: Separate historical achieved milestones from equivalent-resource code comparisons

baseline.selection: Exact immutable image from the original passing 25 new incidents/sec benchmark; already contains earlier async architecture, not pre-feature synchronous main

protocol.sequence: A-B-B-A at 25/sec initially; advance each image independently only after all functional gates pass
protocol.resources: Same release profile: application aggregate 8 CPU / 6400 MiB; PostgreSQL 2 CPU / 1024 MiB; same per-role limits and pool ceilings
protocol.database: Independent clones from one quiescent aged template; record migration versions and whether any candidate migrations are shared with old code
protocol.dependencies: Image-native pinned dependencies; no rebuild or competing local benchmark during timed measurement
protocol.features: Same critical SMTP and pinned Automation fixture; require downstream drain, no acknowledged receipt loss and stable overload accounting
metrics: downstream due count and oldest age
database calls, WAL and lock waits
caveats: Shared Docker VM and unrelated services remain; separate databases do not isolate host resources
Aged synthetic history is not production bloat
A common new schema measures old/new code on that schema, not a native historical installation
Configured provider fanout must be reported explicitly; unconfigured load does not certify all external providers
